title: Paper 2/4: verifiability (declaration timeline, number checks, data terms, archive steps)
body:
## Summary

```diff
 Makefile
+  paper-numbers      # headline numbers from saved results (seconds)
+  paper-reproduce    # re-run both diagnoses from cached data, compare (~50 min)
 src/ctr/
+  paper_numbers.py   # every paper number, keyed, from the result files
 tests/unit/
+  test_paper_numbers.py   # <!--n:KEY-->value<!--/n--> in claim.md / draft.md must match
 docs/paper/
+  preregistration.md # declarations vs first runs, with git + GitHub server times
+  data.md            # accession, licence, data-use terms per dataset
+  archive-steps.md   # release / Zenodo / Software Heritage steps — NOT run
~  claim.md           # numbers tagged; 0.62 -> 0.625
 docs/
~  results.md         # two lines corrected + dated correction note
```

## Evidence

- `make paper-reproduce` (fresh run on this machine, lumencell 0.5.0, plus R1 at `37197c8` via `git archive`): **`91 of 91 numbers reproduce`**.
  - The first attempt failed at R1 because the archive held only `src/`. Fixed by also archiving `benchmarks/`, then re-ran the remaining steps.
- `make lint typecheck test`: 474 passed.
- `test_fresh_run_compares_against_saved`: drop one supported control from the fresh doc → `DIFFERS verdict.r2: saved 27 of 30, fresh 26 of 30`, exit 1.

**Flags from `preregistration.md` (please read):**

| Rows | Flag |
|---|---|
| 1, 3, 5 (real-data gates, both clone-score calibrations) | Order isn't provable server-side. The declaration hit GitHub with the result, or before the event log starts. All three are supplement only. |
| 3 | The run used uncommitted code (the result file says so). |
| 6 (owner ruling H-1, "weak" not capped) | This is a change made after the verification failed. It changes the display only. |
| 9, 10 (the two diagnoses) | The result files record no run time or commit. GitHub proves the declaration merged 21 and 27 minutes before the results were pushed. That the runs started after the merge rests on local file times only. |
| 7 (Sheih) | The data were opened before the declaration, under a recorded freeze rule (headers, barcodes and counts only). |

**From `data.md`:**
- The gastrulation figshare file was reprocessed by a later bioRxiv study (10.1101/2020.12.21.423773), so that study must be cited too.
- Setty 2019's HCA link is dead; the current project is `091cf39b-…`.
- The pancreas h5ad's host states no licence.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Docs, one read-only module, one test and two Makefile targets. No rule, threshold or null changed, and no result file changed.

**Blast Radius:** small

The new test fails if a marked number in `claim.md`/`draft.md` drifts from the result files. That is the intent.

title: Paper 1/4: claim, glossary and scope
body:
## Summary

```diff
 docs/paper/
+├── claim.md   # the claim, glossary, scope, prior work to cite
 ├── literature.md
 ├── diagnosis-verdict.md
 └── diagnosis-clonal.md
```

`claim.md` holds:
- **The claim**, two sentences: (1) the coverage-based verdict rated 27 of 30 controls supported on lumencell 0.5.0 (the old 28 of 31 is in a footnote, with why it doesn't reproduce); (2) Sheih 2020: the score is under half against the time-point shuffle in the point estimate of all 12 runs, two intervals reach 0.62 and 0.77, and k-means comes within 0.05 (lift interval above zero in 4 runs, below zero in 3).
- **What is already known**, with the papers that must be cited. The claim is narrowed to the two things the search did not find.
- **Scope**, the **disclosed `hand_verdict` deviation**, the **glossary**, and the **wording rules**.
- **How the binding points check against the pages.** All hold; three need careful wording (see below).

## Evidence

Every number was re-read from the result files, not copied from the pages:

- `diagnosis-verdict-2026-11-23.json`: `reproduce_on_0_5_0.n_controls_supported` 27, `C1@fixed.passes` 28, all-four combo 2 (`matrix_q`) and 4 (`matrix_min`)
- `diagnosis-clonal-2026-11-23.json` `sheih_bootstrap`: R intervals for NHL-7 palantir and scfates_ppt are [0.179, 0.625] and [0.245, 0.770]; lift intervals above zero in 4 runs and wholly below in 3 (same runs as the page)

Wording caveats for review:
1. The "2" is out of the **31 recorded** controls. The headline is 27 of **30**, so don't pair the two counts.
2. "Reads coverage alone" is true of the 31-run check. On Sheih the rule also reads the clone check (C5).
3. "Time doesn't explain the drop" holds only for time structure *of the simulated kind*.
4. `docs/results.md` says "time-point **or pseudotime** null below half in every run". Against the pseudotime shuffle that's false (CLL-1 paga_dpt is 0.695 to 0.363). The draft must not copy it.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Docs only. No code, rule, threshold or result changes.

**Blast Radius:** none

title: Results: clonal-confound diagnosis (Q2)
body:
Results under the merged declaration (#5). Write-up: `docs/paper/diagnosis-clonal.md`; numbers: `benchmarks/results/diagnosis-clonal-2026-11-23.json`.

- Declared outcome: D1 fails, so time structure of this kind does not explain the Sheih drop. With time-only clones, eta against the within-patient null stays at 0.013 or below, although that null's p over-rejects (15 to 18 of 40 against a bound of 6 at sigma 0.1). With real signal, eta against the time-point null keeps 99 to 100% of eta against the within-patient null.
- Sheih per run, with clone-bootstrap intervals: recorded eta reproduces exactly; 'under half in 12 of 12' holds for the point estimates only (NHL-7 palantir and scfates_ppt intervals reach 0.62 and 0.77); the k-means lift is within +-0.05 as point values but not as intervals.
- Daniel 2022 declined by the owner; not run.

title: Results: verdict-verification diagnosis (Q1)
body:
Results under the merged declaration (#4). Answer in `docs/paper/diagnosis-verdict.md`, numbers in `benchmarks/results/diagnosis-verdict-2026-11-23.json`.

- (a) bug refuted: 0 of 67 verdicts differ from a re-derivation.
- (b) bad controls refuted: all four kinds separate from trees on the four-point defect.
- (c) permissive rule supported: coverage alone passes 28 of 31; all four criteria at tree bars pass 2.
- (d) real property not supported as declared (ordering is real, stability is not in the tree range).
- R1 does not reproduce exactly at 37197c8 (3 two_groups scfates runs now run); the paper number is 27 of 30 on lumencell 0.5.0.

One deviation to review: the reproduce harness counts supported controls with `hand_verdict` because 37197c8's `verdict()` has no `verified` argument.

title: Pin lumencell 0.5 and use its packaged policy files
body:
- `pyproject.toml`: `lumencell[all]>=0.5,<0.6` from PyPI. The git source is gone.
- `src/ctr/gates.py`: the baseline and the tool's `thresholds.toml` now come from the installed `lumencell/bench/policy`. `load_thresholds()` deep-merges this repo's file over the tool's, so a key set here wins.
- `benchmarks/thresholds.toml` is cut down to what research owns: `[real.*]`, `[case_study.*]`, `[clonal.calibration*]`, `[tree_support.calibration]` and `[tree_support.verification]`. The changelog keeps the research entries word for word. The three tool-only entries are dropped; they are still in lumencell's file.
- `benchmarks/baseline.json` is deleted. Its content was identical to the packaged one.
- `tests/unit/test_gates.py` covers the merge and the trimmed file's tables.

Check: `load_thresholds()` equals the old full `thresholds.toml` on main, value for value. Lint, format and mypy are clean, and 452 fast tests pass, including `test_reference_scores.py`. The source label in `ctr.reference` stays `benchmarks/baseline.json @ <commit>`, because the tool's `reference_scores.json` uses that exact string. The slow calibration tests were not rerun: the config they read is unchanged.

title: Declare the clonal-confound diagnosis (Q2), before any check runs
body:
Declaration PR for question 2: is the clonal agreement score confounded by time? Merge before any result PR.

**Adds, new files only**
- `docs/paper/declaration-clonal-confound.md`
- `src/ctr/diagnosis_clonal.py` and `tests/unit/test_diagnosis_clonal.py` (toy data only)

**What the declaration settles by reading**
- The existing calibration already shows that N1 is confounded by pseudotime depth (`depth_only/N1`: 200 of 200 rejections with no lineage signal) and that N2a fixes it. It does not answer this question: it stores p-values only (no eta), and N3 (time-point strata) was never calibrated because the generator has no time points.
- So section 2 declares a synthetic check: four arms (no structure, time only, lineage only, both), two time-noise levels, 40 fresh seeds (600-639), N1, N2 and N3 scored with the runtime definitions, and four outcomes fixed in advance.
- Section 3 declares a clone bootstrap (500 replicates, 100 permutations) for all 12 Sheih runs, per-run values rather than counts, and the k-means lift.
- Section 4 gives the reasons Daniel 2022 cannot serve as a confirming second dataset. It is not run.

**Not run.** No score has been computed. No threshold, seed, null or definition is changed.

title: Declare the verdict-verification diagnosis (Q1), before any check runs
body:
Declaration PR for question 1: why did the verdict rule rate 28 of 31 negative controls supported? Merge this before any result PR.

**Adds, new files only**
- `docs/paper/declaration-verdict-diagnosis.md`: the four explanations (bug, bad controls, permissive rule, real property), the reproduction check R1 to R3, decision rules, claim templates.
- `src/ctr/diagnosis_verdict.py` and `tests/unit/test_diagnosis_verdict.py`: the checks, tested on toy data only.

**Two things the declaration settles from the repo, no run needed**
- The verified rule reads coverage alone (every tau is None, C5 does not apply), so "tree-support" is the wrong name for what failed. The literature note is right about this.
- The literature note is only partly right on "not declared". `[tree_support.verification]` (seeds 3-5, controls, max 0) was declared in `fdc200a`, 2.5 hours before the run. Only the count 31 (36 runs minus 5 failed) was not declared, and there is no public registry entry.

**Not run.** Nothing here has touched the recorded files or fresh data. The doc says what I had already read, so (a) and (c) are not claimed as blind tests.

No threshold, seed, control or null is changed. `pyproject.toml` and `thresholds.toml` are untouched.

title: Literature check for the planned short paper
body:
Adds `docs/paper/literature.md`, a literature check for the working claim of the planned short paper. Research only, no code changes.

**Verdict: partly known.**

- **Already published:**
  - TCR or lineage-barcode checks of trajectories: STARTRAC, LRT, Clonotrace, PhyloTrajectory, Wilson 2022, Weinreb 2020.
  - Clone-label shuffles within strata: Swift 2023, and the STARTRAC within-patient shuffle.
  - Negative controls for a trajectory-presence statistic: Tenha and Song 2022.
- **Plausibly new:**
  1. Scoring trajectory lineages against time-point-stratified and pseudotime-stratified clone nulls plus a k-means baseline, on public human CAR-T data.
  2. Reporting that a verdict rule failed its negative-control check (28 of 31 rated supported).

The file also flags where the current claim sentence does not match the repo:

- The rule that failed reads coverage and clonal support only. It is not a tree-likeness rule.
- "Pre-registered": the dated declaration covers the Sheih plan only.
- "Mostly vanished": against the within-patient null, p stays 0.000999 in every run.
- "Depth" in the repo means pseudotime decile, not sequencing depth.

The file proposes revised wording for the claim.

**Checks:**

- 25 papers were checked against Crossref or Europe PMC. Most checks read the abstract only.
- 8 items could not be opened and are listed as unverified.
- I re-checked 4 DOIs against Crossref while reviewing.
- The bioRxiv rules are cited page by page. Whether an unaffiliated author is accepted could not be confirmed (bioRxiv asks for an affiliation "so there is an entity providing oversight"). Ask bioRxiv before submitting.

Do not merge yet.
